title: Claude Opus 5.5 lands 20% cheaper — and thinking can't be turned off
summary: Anthropic's Opus 5.5 and OpenAI's GPT-6 Sol and Luna shipped ninety minutes apart, cutting prices in opposite directions — and Opus 5.5 removed the thinking switch entirely. Plus the FAA's SMART system goes live in Washington airspace as phase one of a published four-phase ladder.

topics: Claude Opus 5.5 (released 2026-09-22): $4/$20 per MTok versus Opus 5's $5/$25, cache reads $0.20 (60% cheaper), 1M-token context, 128K max output, adaptive thinking always on with manual extended-thinking budgets 'not accepted on later models'; Anthropic's cost-per-task post (2.8M input tokens in an illustrative 40-turn session, ~$1.62 input at 90% cache hit rate, ~$0.99 at 96%, 60K output = $1.20, ~$1.02 for the same task in 25 turns); Terminal-Bench 4.0 66.4 vs 52.3, CursorBench 57.8 vs 46.6, FrontierCode 54.4 vs 48.0 at max effort; containment-boundary circumvention attempts 85% less often than Opus 5, tied with Fable 5.1 on prompt injection, external testing by METR and Frontier Design; Simon Willison reports max effort consuming the full 128K output limit and returning nothing

OpenAI GPT-6 Sol and Luna (2026-09-22, ~90 minutes after Opus 5.5): Sol $2/$0.20 cached/$10 per MTok, Luna $0.10/$0.01/$0.50, both ~1.05M context and 128K max output; the 6-series priced at half the 5.6 equivalents on caching and inference improvements; OpenAI's internal factuality evaluation claims Sol 'makes about half as many mistakes as its predecessor, reaching Astra-level reliability'; OpenAI claims the pair substantially outperform Fable and Opus; Epoch AI measures the cost of a fixed performance level falling 47% per quarter (13x/year) since 2023 across five math/science/games benchmarks, faster than electricity, compute, batteries or DNA sequencing ever fell

FAA SMART (Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes and Trajectories) entering limited operation in Washington airspace (Reagan National, Dulles, BWI) the week of 2026-09-21: 12-year, $875M contract to Air Space Intelligence awarded June 2026 over Palantir and Thales; 200 data streams including controller staffing; flow management rather than separation; conflict-prediction horizon extended from 15 minutes to two hours via 4D modelling; dynamic altitude-specific weather replacing static ground-level data; Leeham's four-phase framework from advisory-only (phase one, no real-time control authority) to real-time flight-path coordination (phase four); Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy: 'We are not outsourcing aviation to AI'

threads.name: Frontier model price war
threads.status: Anthropic and OpenAI cut prices 90 minutes apart on 2026-09-22; Opus 5.5 at $4/$20, GPT-6 Luna at $0.10/$0.50, Grok 4.7 at $2/$6 the day before
threads.arc: What began as per-token undercutting has moved to cost-per-task claims and always-on reasoning, so the headline price and the invoice now diverge; Epoch's 13x-a-year curve is the backdrop

dives.story: Opus 5.5, cost per task, and the removal of the thinking switch
dives.why_it_matters: Anyone budgeting an agentic coding deployment needs to know that the 40% saving is a cost-per-task claim driven by cache hit rate and turn count rather than the 20% list-price cut, and that with thinking no longer disableable the spend per call has no ceiling they control.

dives.story: GPT-6 Sol and Luna and what ten cents a million does to architecture
dives.why_it_matters: Teams who built cheap-tier routing and retrieval specifically to avoid frontier token costs now have to re-examine those designs, because at $0.10 per million input tokens the filter can cost more to maintain than the calls it was protecting against.

dives.story: FAA SMART and the four-phase ladder from advisory to authority
dives.why_it_matters: Anyone deploying AI decision support in a regulated setting should see how the advisory phase generates the evidence used to justify removing the human — a record measured on the human-plus-machine pair that stops being valid once the human leaves.

repeat_coverage.new_development: Within a week a local llama.cpp reimplementation, a benchmark project and a from-scratch clone reproducing the behaviour from any model's log-probabilities have appeared, which puts the packaging-versus-architecture question on evidence rather than argument.

lore.note: Alan staked out that a model which thinks by default is probably right, but that a control you cannot turn off is a cost you cannot cap — explicitly separating the two claims and saying they shipped together in one release. He held it against Ada's register-allocation analogy without conceding, and Ada did not concede either.
